title: Notation
body_md:
We will use                                                                                      
uppercase calligraphic font $\mathcal{A}$ for operators. Given Hilbert spaces $X$ and $Y$, $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the set of bounded linear operators from $X$ to $Y$. We denote the Hilbert adjoint by $\mathcal{A}^* \in \mathcal{L}(Y,X)$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
 $L_{\infty}^{n}[\Omega]$, and $L_2^n[\Omega]$ are the spaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$--valued Lebesgue bounded, and Lebesgue square-integrable functions, respectively, on the domain $\Omega$,          
with the standard inner product. $W^{n}_d[\Omega]$ is the Sobolev space of $d$ times $L_2$--differentiable $\mathbb{R}^{n}$--valued functions on $\Omega$. \vspace{-2 mm}

label: def:piesol
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:piesol}
Given $\mathcal{T,A,B, C, H}\in\pmb{\Pi}$,                                                      
$\{x,z\}$ is a \textbf{solution of $G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{H})$} if                
$\mathcal{T}x$ is Fréchet differentiable, and                                                                                                     
$\{z, x$, $w$,$v\}$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:PIE}.

label: def:wellposed
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wellposed}
We say $G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{H})$ is well-posed if, for every $w\in L_2$ and $v \in \mathbb{R}^{n_v}$, there exists a solution $\{x,z\}$ of  $G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{H})$.

label: lem:intertwining
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $x,v$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:primal_aux}, and $\bar v,\bar x$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:dualPIE}. Define $V(t)
=\left\langle
\bar x(t),\mathcal T x(T-t)
\right\rangle$ for $t \in [0,T]$. Then
\begin{align*}
\dot V(t)&=\left\langle \mathcal T^*\dot{\bar x}(t),x(T-t)\right\rangle
-
\left\langle \bar x(t),\mathcal T\dot x(T-t)\right\rangle
\\
&=
\left\langle 
\mathcal A^*\bar x(t)
+\mathcal C^*\bar v(t),x(T-t)\right\rangle-
\left\langle \bar x(t),\mathcal A x(T-t)\right\rangle\\
&=
\left\langle \bar v(t), \mathcal{C}x(T-t) \right\rangle.
\end{align*}
Hence, integrating in $t$ over $[0,T]$ we have 
\begin{align*}
&V(T)-V(0)=\int_0^T\left\langle \bar v(t), \mathcal{C}x(T-t) \right\rangle dt\\
&=-\int_T^0\left\langle \bar v(T-s), \mathcal{C}x(s) \right\rangle ds=\int_0^T\left\langle \bar v(T-s), \mathcal{C}x(s) \right\rangle ds
\end{align*}
where we used the change of variables $s=T-t$. Now from Eqn.~\eqref{eq:primal_aux}, we have $\mathcal{T} x(0)= \mathcal B v$ and from Eqn.~\eqref{eq:dualPIE}, we have $\mathcal{T}^*\bar x(0)=0$. Thus
\begin{align*}
&\bigl(\mathcal{B}^* \bar x(T) \bigr)^T v=\left\langle \bar x(T),\mathcal{B} v\right\rangle=\left\langle \bar x(T),\mathcal{T} x(0)\right\rangle\\&
=\left\langle \bar x(T),\mathcal{T} x(0)\right\rangle-\left\langle \mathcal{T}^*\bar x(0),x(T)\right\rangle\\
&=\left\langle \bar x(T),\mathcal{T} x(0)\right\rangle-\left\langle \bar x(0),\mathcal{T}x(T)\right\rangle=V(T)-V(0)\\
&=\int_0^T\left\langle \bar v(T-t),\mathcal{C} x(t)\right\rangle dt
\end{align*}
as desired.

label: thm:dualnorm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dualnorm}
Given $\mathcal{T,A,B,C}\in \pmb{\Pi}$, let $G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})$ and $G(\mathcal{T}^*,\mathcal{A}^*,\mathcal{C}^*,\mathcal{B}^*,0)$ be well-posed. Then we have that
\[
    \|G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})\|_{2,i}
    =
    \|G(\mathcal{T}^*,\mathcal{A}^*,\mathcal{C}^*,\mathcal{B}^*,0)\|_{\infty,2}.
\]

label: thm:LPI_2,i
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove that if the inequalities hold for some $\mathcal{P}\succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$, then $\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2 \leq \gamma$, recalling that
\[
\|G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})\|_{2,i}:= \sup_{T>0}   \sup_{\substack{v,z,\mathbf{x}\text{satisfy~\eqref{eq:primal_aux}}\\ \left\lVert{v}\right\rVert_2=1}} \left\lVert{z}\right\rVert_{L_2[0,T)}.
\]
Suppose there exist $\mathcal{P}\succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$ satisfying                            
Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi1b}. 
For any $T>0$, let $z, x, v$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:primal_aux} for $t\in[0,T]$, given some initial condition with $\left\lVert{v}\right\rVert_2=1$. Define the storage functional $V(x(t))=\left\langle  x(t),\mathcal{T^*PT}x(t)\right\rangle_{L_2[a,b]}$. Since $\mathcal{P}$ is coercive, $V(x)\ge \epsilon \left\lVert{\mathcal{T}x}\right\rVert^2$ for any $x\in L_2$. Then, taking time derivative along solutions of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:primal_aux}, we have that
    \begin{align*}
        \dot V(x(t))&=\left\langle  x(t),(\mathcal{A^*PT+T^*PA}), x(t)\right\rangle_{L_2[a,b]},
    \end{align*}
    and, since $\mathcal{P}$ satisfies Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi1b}, we further have that
    \[
    \dot V( x(t)) \leq -\left\langle x(t),\mathcal{C^*C} x(t)\right\rangle_{L_2[a,b]}.
    \]
    Integrating $\dot{V}$ w.r.t. $t$ over $[0,T]$,                                                                            
    we have that
    \begin{align*}
  \left\lVert{z}\right\rVert_{L_2[0,T]}^2&=\int_0^T\left\langle x(s),\mathcal{C^*C}x(s)\right\rangle ds \\
    &\leq V(x(0))- V(x(T))\leq V(x(0))\\
    &=\left\langle x(0),\mathcal{T^*PT}x(0)\right\rangle=\left\langle \mathcal{B} v,\mathcal{PB} v\right\rangle
    \end{align*}
                              
        
                                                    
        
Then, since $\mathcal{P}, \gamma$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi1b}, we have that
   \[
    \left\lVert{z}\right\rVert_{L_2[0,T]}^2 \leq \bigl|\left\langle \mathcal{B} v, \mathcal{PB} v\right\rangle\bigr| \Bigr|\leq  \gamma \left\lVert{v}\right\rVert_2^2=\gamma.
   \]
    Since the inequality holds uniformly for any $T>0$ and solution of Eqn. \eqref{eq:primal_aux}, by the definition of the impulse-to-energy norm, we conclude that
$\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T,A},0,C,B)}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2 \leq \gamma$, as desired.

title: Proof
body_md:
As before, we first prove that if                            
    Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi6b_} hold for some $\mathcal{P}\succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$, then $\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T^*,A^*},\mathcal{C}^*,\mathcal{B}^*,0)}\right\rVert_{\infty,2}^2 \leq \gamma$, and use the duality result in Thm.~\ref{thm:dualnorm}.                                                                                                 
    Suppose there exist $\mathcal{P}\succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$ satisfying                             
    Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi6b_}.
    Now, let $\mathcal{T'=T^*}$, $\mathcal{A'=A^*}$, $\mathcal{B'=C^*}$, and $\mathcal{C'=B^*}$. Since $\mathcal{T,A,B,C} \in \pmb{\Pi} \subset \mathcal{L}(X)$ and $(A^*)^*=A$ for any $A\in \mathcal{L}(X)$, we can verify that the conditions of Thm.~\ref{thm:LPI_inf,2} hold for $\mathcal{T}',\mathcal{A}',\mathcal{B}',\mathcal{C}'$ since
    \begin{align*}
                 \begin{bmatrix} -\gamma I & \mathcal{(B')^*PT'}\\ \mathcal{(T')^* P B'} & \mathcal{(A')^*PT'+(T')^*PA'} \end{bmatrix} &\preccurlyeq0\;\\               
        \mathcal{(C')^*C'}-\mathcal{(T')^*PT'}&
        \preccurlyeq 0,
    \end{align*}    
    implying \(\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T}',\mathcal{A}',\mathcal{B}',\mathcal{C}',0)}\right\rVert_{\infty,2}^2\leq \gamma.\)
Now, from Thm.~\ref{thm:dualnorm}, we can conclude that
\begin{align*}
    \gamma&\ge \left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T}'\!,\!\mathcal{A}'\!,\!\mathcal{B}'\!,\mathcal{C}',0)}\right\rVert_{\infty,2}^2\\
    &=\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{(T')^*\!,\!(A')^*}\!,0,\!\mathcal{(B')^*\!,\!(C')^*})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2\\
    &=\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{(T^*)^*,(A^*)^*},0,\mathcal{(C^*)^*,(B^*)^*})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2\\
    &=\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T,A},0,\mathcal{C,B})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2.
\end{align*}

label: thm:LPIs_2,i_dilated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove each statement separately

\noindent \textbf{Proof of $1)$}:  Suppose $1)$ holds for some $\mathcal{P} \succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$.                              
Then, $\mathcal{P} \in \pmb{\Pi} \subset \mathcal{L}(X)$, and $\mathcal{P},\gamma$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi2b}. Now, we apply Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} using $\mathcal{U}=-\mathcal{C} \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, $\mathcal{R}=-(\mathcal{A^*PT+T^*PA}) \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, and $\mathcal{S} = \gamma I \in \mathcal{L}(X)$. Since $\mathcal{S} \succcurlyeq \epsilon I$ for any $\epsilon\in(0,\gamma]$, the conditions of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} are satisfied. Then, we have that 
\[
\begin{bmatrix} -\mathcal{S}&-\mathcal{U}\\-\mathcal{U}^*&-\mathcal{R} \end{bmatrix}= \begin{bmatrix} -\gamma I  & \mathcal{C}\\\mathcal{C}^*& \mathcal{A^*PT+T^*PA}  \end{bmatrix}\preccurlyeq0,
\]
\[
 \text{and hence}\,\begin{bmatrix} \mathcal{S}&\mathcal{U}\\\mathcal{U}^*&\mathcal{R} \end{bmatrix}\succcurlyeq0.
\]
Then, statement 1) of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} holds. This implies
\[
-\Bigl( \mathcal{A^*PT+T^*PA+C^*C}\frac{1}{\gamma}\Bigr)=\mathcal{R-U^*}\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathcal{U} \succcurlyeq 0.
\]

 Furthermore, $\mathcal{P},\gamma$ satisfy Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi2b}.
       
                    
                                                                                                                                                              
              
    Now, we apply Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} using $\mathcal{U}=\mathcal{PB} \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, $\mathcal{R}=\gamma I \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, and $\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{P} \in \mathcal{L}(X)$. Then, since $\mathcal{S} =\mathcal{P} \succcurlyeq \epsilon I$, the conditions of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} are satisfied. Then, we have that
    \[
    \begin{bmatrix} \mathcal{S}&\mathcal{U}\\\mathcal{U}^*&\mathcal{R} \end{bmatrix}= \begin{bmatrix} \mathcal{P} & \mathcal{PB}\\\mathcal{B^*P}&\gamma I \end{bmatrix}\succcurlyeq0,
    \]
    and hence, statement 1) of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} holds. This implies
    \[
 \gamma I -\mathcal{B^*PB} = \gamma I -\mathcal{B^*PP}^{-1}\mathcal{PB}=\mathcal{R-U^*}\mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathcal{U} \succcurlyeq 0.
\]
  Next, let $\hat{\mathcal{P}} =\mathcal{P}\gamma$. Then, we have that $\hat{\mathcal{P}} \succcurlyeq \gamma \epsilon I$ and
 \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{A^*\hat{P}T+T^* \hat{P} A+C^*C}  &\preccurlyeq0,                                    
        \; \gamma^2 I-\mathcal{B^*}\hat{\mathcal{P}}\mathcal{B} \succcurlyeq 0,                   
    \end{align*}
and hence $\mathcal{\hat P}=\mathcal{P} \gamma$, and $\gamma^2$ satisfy the conditions of Thm.~\ref{thm:LPI_2,i}. This implies that $\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2 \leq \gamma^2$,  and hence
$\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})}\right\rVert_{2,i} \leq \gamma$, as desired.

                    
 \noindent \textbf{Proof of $2)$}: Next, we prove statement $2)$ by showing that if there exist $\mathcal{P} \succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma >0$ satisfying $2)$, then $\|G(\mathcal{T}^*,\mathcal{A}^*,\mathcal{C}^*,\mathcal{B}^*,0)\|_{\infty,2} \leq \gamma$, recalling that
\[\|G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C},0)\|_{\infty,2}=    \sup_{T >0}
   \sup_{\substack{v,x\, \text{satisfy~\eqref{eq:dualPIE}}\\\left\lVert{v}\right\rVert_{L_2[0,T]}=1} } \|z (T)\|.\]
                                                                           
                 
                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                             
                  
      Suppose there exist $\mathcal{P}\succcurlyeq \epsilon I, \gamma>0$ satisfying                            
      Eqn.~\eqref{eq:lpi3b}.                                                                                                         
                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                   
               
                    
                                                                                                                                    
                  
                                                                   
        Now, we apply Lem.~\ref{lem:schur}, using $\mathcal{U} =\mathcal{B^*} \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, $\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{TPT^*} \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, and $\mathcal{S}=\gamma I \in \mathcal{L}(X)$. Since $\gamma I \succcurlyeq \epsilon I$ for any $\epsilon\in(0,\gamma]$, the conditions of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} are satisfied.        
        We have      
\[
  \begin{bmatrix} \mathcal{S}&\mathcal{U}\\\mathcal{U}^*&\mathcal{R} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} \gamma I & \mathcal{B}^*\\\mathcal{B} & \mathcal{TPT^*} \end{bmatrix}\succcurlyeq 0,
\]        
    and hence, statement 1) of Lem.~\ref{lem:schur} holds. This implies
    \[
                                                 
     \mathcal{TPT^*} -\gamma^{-1}\mathcal{BB^*} =\mathcal{R}- \mathcal{U}^* \mathcal{S}^{-1}\mathcal{U}  \succcurlyeq 0.
    \]
                
                         
                                                                             
                  
 Next, let $\hat{\mathcal{P}} =\mathcal{P}\gamma$. Then, we have that $\hat{\mathcal{P}} \succcurlyeq \gamma \epsilon I$, and
\begin{align*}
          \begin{bmatrix} -\gamma^2 I & \mathcal{C\hat PT^*}\\ \mathcal{T \hat P C^*} & \mathcal{A\hat PT^*+T\hat PA^*} \end{bmatrix} &\preccurlyeq0, \;\mathcal{T\hat PT^*} -\mathcal{BB^*}\succcurlyeq 0,
\end{align*}
and hence $\mathcal{\hat P}=\mathcal{P} \gamma$, and $\gamma^2$ satisfy the conditions of Cor.~\ref{cor:LPI_2,i_dual}. This implies $\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})}\right\rVert_{2,i}^2\leq \gamma^2$, and hence $\left\lVert{G(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{A},0,\mathcal{C},\mathcal{B})}\right\rVert_{2,i}\leq \gamma$ is proven.

title: Example
body_md:
First consider the scalar, single delay system, where the non-zero matrices are $A_1=-1$,                                
                $B=2$, and $C_0=2$, with the delay $\tau = 0.5$. This system has an analytic bound for the $H_2$ norm, which is $3.6724$.
head: manual

title: Example
body_md:
Next, consider the two-delay system with $\tau_1 = \pi/10$, $\tau_2 = 1$, so that the delays are incommensurate, and
				\begin{align*}
					&A_0 = \begin{bmatrix} 
						-1 & 1 & 2\\
						1 & -3 & 2\\
						0 & 0 & -1
					 \end{bmatrix},\qquad  A_1 = \frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix} 
						-3 & 0 & 1\\
						1 & -2 & 0\\
						0 & 2 & -2
					 \end{bmatrix},\\
					& A_2 =  \frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix} 
						-4 & 1 & 0\\
						0 & -2 & 1\\
						2 & 1 & -3
					 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{bmatrix} 	1 \\ 1 \\1 \end{bmatrix}, \; C_0 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 &1  \end{bmatrix}.
				\end{align*}
				The method in~\cite{jarlebring2011} and the bounds from the LPIs agree to four significant figures. However, 10th order Pad\'e approximation yields a           
                higher value of of $3.9275$ for the $H_2$--norm.
